excluded_blocks.block: SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md#Untrusted code in a privileged workflow
excluded_blocks.reason: No CI workflows exist in the repository.
No plugin/extension loading and no updater/signing surface exists.

local_checks.invariant: Every build input determining image/artifact content is bound to a reviewed immutable identity, or a lower-trust writer able to change it is named with the consuming trusted build.
local_checks.result: Frontend resolution is bound: pnpm-lock.yaml carries sha512 integrity for every package and the Dockerfile runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Backend resolution is NOT bound: pyproject.toml uses open-ended '>=' ranges with no lockfile/hashes, so backend/Dockerfile `pip install -e .` resolves fresh versions each build. Base images use mutable minor tags. The dev extra declares `httpx2>=2`, a name no source file imports and which no hash pins. frontend/.dockerignore has no `.env*` rule while the Dockerfile does `COPY . .`, but no .env* exists in frontend/ and the only consumed var (VITE_API_BASE) is non-secret.

hardening_notes: Base images use mutable tags, not digests: python:3.12-slim, node:22-alpine, nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine.
Backend runtime dependencies use open-ended '>=' ranges with no Python lockfile or hash pinning; the built image is not reproducibility/integrity bound.
frontend/.dockerignore omits `.env*` while the Dockerfile does `COPY . .`; a developer-local frontend/.env would enter the build context and Vite would inline VITE_ values (non-secret today).
frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml sets minimumReleaseAgeExclude without a matching minimumReleaseAge, so the intended pnpm release-cooldown is a no-op.
frontend/Dockerfile runs `npm install -g pnpm@11.10.0` from the public registry (version-pinned, not hash-pinned).

final_decisions.note: Source-grounded dependency-integrity hypothesis pending an offline/hosted resolution observation.

excluded_blocks.reason: No browser sink in the settings module.

local_checks.invariant: Every env-derived setting has a safe fallback and invalid values fail at startup, not at request time.
local_checks.result: database_url/cors_origins/seed_on_start/log_level have safe defaults; cors_origins only splits a comma list; log_level falls back to INFO. GAP: app_tz is materialized lazily in Settings.tz, so an invalid APP_TZ is accepted at boot then raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError on the first request that computes current_month()/serializes a datetime -> per-request 500. Operator-controlled, self-impact -> hardening.

local_checks.invariant: A setting has a single effective source of truth and app_env changes the runtime posture where claimed.
local_checks.result: Two inert fields: app_env is read nowhere (no production profile exists), and seed_on_start is never consumed; the effective seed gate is the entrypoint's literal string compare, so a truthy-but-not-lowercase value parses True in Settings yet silently does not seed.

hardening_notes: config.py: APP_TZ is only materialized lazily in Settings.tz; an invalid timezone is accepted at startup and then 500s every request that computes current_month() or serializes a datetime. Add a field validator so a bad timezone fails at boot.
config.py: app_env is read but never used; no production profile rejects a wildcard CORS_ORIGINS, disables /api/docs + /api/openapi.json, or forces SEED_ON_START off.
config.py: seed_on_start is dead config; the effective gate is entrypoint.sh's string compare, so 'True'/'1' parses truthy in Settings yet does not seed. Collapse to one source of truth.

excluded_blocks.reason: No cookies or ambient credentials exist, so browser session fixation/CSRF is structurally absent.
No JWT/OAuth/SAML/MFA/passkey/token surface exists.

local_checks.invariant: CORSMiddleware must not reflect or weakly match Origin while allowing credentials against sensitive responses.
local_checks.result: cors_origins is an explicit list (default ['http://localhost:5173']) parsed from CORS_ORIGINS with no '*' and no allow_origin_regex, so Starlette can only echo a listed origin. No cookies/session/HTTP auth exist, so the credentialed path is inert by default. Failure requires an operator to set CORS_ORIGINS='*' (not source-visible).

hardening_notes: allow_credentials=True is set although the app writes no cookies and uses no HTTP auth; dropping it removes the credentialed-CORS anti-pattern entirely.
config.app_env is read but never used: no production profile rejects a wildcard CORS_ORIGINS, disables /api/docs and /api/openapi.json, or forces SEED_ON_START off.
/api/docs and /api/openapi.json are always served with no config toggle, exposing a full API map on the unauthenticated surface.

final_decisions.note: Independently validated and refuted; retained in findings.json so future runs do not repeat the unsupported claim.

excluded_blocks.reason: No authorization decision is made on the month/date path.
No SQL string construction: month/date values are bound parameters or Python-level filters.

local_checks.invariant: month_bounds rejects malformed month keys with 422 and produces a correct half-open range across ordinary year boundaries.
local_checks.result: parse_month requires 4-digit year + zero-padded month 01..12; shift_month uses floor integer arithmetic (2024-01 -1 -> 2023-12). All routers pass the range to bound SQL predicates (date >= start, < end).

local_checks.invariant: No year value accepted by parse_month/shift_month/valid_date_str can make router date construction raise an uncaught ValueError.
local_checks.result: Reproduced in an OS sandbox (bwrap, no net, empty env, ro target, scratch-only writes, rlimits): month_bounds('0000-01') and ('0000-12') raise uncaught ValueError('year 0 is out of range'); '9999-12' raises uncaught ValueError from the unguarded second parse_month('10000-01'); valid_date_str('0000-01-01') is True while date.fromisoformat raises. Each is HTTP 500 returned only to the requester (self-impact, no mutation) -> recorded as hardening, not a cross-boundary finding.

hardening_notes: backend/app/routers/__init__.py: a month key of 0000-01/0000-12 passes parse_month then date(0,1,1) raises an uncaught ValueError -> HTTP 500 (self-impact). Reject year 0000 in parse_month or move date() inside the guarded try. Regression: GET /api/movements?month=0000-01 must be 422.

backend/app/routers/__init__.py: '9999-12' makes shift_month emit a 5-digit year; the second parse_month is outside try/except and raises uncaught ValueError -> 500. Validate the shifted key inside the same guarded block.

backend/app/routers/movements.py: valid_date_str accepts year 0000 but the later date.fromisoformat raises uncaught ValueError -> 500 on POST/PATCH /api/movements. Require year >= 0001. Regression: POST with date '0000-01-01' must be 422.
Sibling divergence: movement CRUD rejects notes > 140 chars with 422 while /api/data/import silently truncates; both bounded and safe, but the two siblings should agree.

excluded_blocks.reason: Single-user store with no authentication by design; no tenant/owner dimension exists.
Budget reads/writes use bound parameters and primary-key lookups; no string SQL is constructed.

local_checks.invariant: Every budget write path enforces validate_cap and rejects non-gasto categories; no path bypasses the control.
local_checks.result: Holds. put_budget calls validate_cap then gates category.type=='gasto' before upsert; the import path enforces equivalent bounds and never persists 0; delete_budget only removes. DB CHECK ck_budgets_cap_positive is the backstop.

local_checks.invariant: get_budgets computes pct/status/totals without division-by-zero or integer overflow for any stored state.
local_checks.result: Holds. pct guarded by cap>0; totals are Python ints; SUM(int4)->bigint in PostgreSQL; cap bounded to 2^31-1 at write; budget_status uses integer cross-multiplication.

local_checks.invariant: put_budget upsert is atomic under concurrent writes.
local_checks.result: Does not hold: get-then-add with no ON CONFLICT; two concurrent first-PUTs both INSERT and one commit raises IntegrityError -> 500 for one requester. Single-user/single-container default means it is not realized -> hardening.

hardening_notes: budgets.py: put_budget is a non-atomic get-or-create upsert; two concurrent first-PUTs for the same category both observe None and one raises IntegrityError -> 500. Not realized under the single-instance default. Use ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE or catch IntegrityError.

excluded_blocks.reason: Movements are hard-deleted (DELETE removes the row); there is no soft-delete or tombstone state to bypass.
Single-user store with no per-resource authorization; every caller has the same authority by design.
The app registers no service worker, so no cached export copy can outlive logout or account switch.

local_checks.invariant: GET /api/data/export discloses only records the caller is authorized for (no cross-principal/tenant scope expansion).
local_checks.result: No finding: single-tenant store with no per-resource authorization, so export cannot include another principal's data; the tenant-isolation class is structurally absent.

local_checks.invariant: Export excludes soft-deleted/draft/private content or pruned history above the caller's access.
local_checks.result: No finding: Movement has no soft-delete/tombstone column; DELETE removes the row, and no draft/history/revision state exists.

local_checks.invariant: Import/restore does not create records that bypass normal validation or overwrite state the caller cannot write.
local_checks.result: No data-isolation finding: import validation matches the CRUD rules and the single owner has full write authority by design.

local_checks.invariant: Export response size is bounded by the request.
local_checks.result: Resource property (not data-leakage): export materializes the whole movements table and serializes it into one JSONResponse with no cap; same root cause as the import-merge read candidate, tracked there.

excluded_blocks.reason: json.loads over a <=5 MB byte-capped body is linear; deep nesting raises RecursionError and is caught and mapped to 422.
The 5 MB byte cap is applied before any parsing, so expensive work cannot start before the size gate.
No multi-tenant records exist to scope per item; import targets the single owner's store.

local_checks.invariant: Declared Content-Length above 5 MB and any real streamed byte count above 5 MB are rejected with 413 before parsing.
local_checks.result: Holds: data.py declared check (~line 38) and streamed accumulation check (~line 45) both raise 413; the integration smoke test asserts declared 11 MB -> 413.

local_checks.invariant: The import payload is bounded per item (<=20000 movements; amount 1..MAX_CENTS; category must match category type).
local_checks.result: Holds: the list cap and per-item checks are present; no path lets a value exceed PostgreSQL INTEGER range.

local_checks.invariant: Every date string accepted by _validate_payload can be consumed by the apply step (valid_date_str agrees with date.fromisoformat).
local_checks.result: FAILS at the boundary: valid_date_str('0000-01-01') is True but date.fromisoformat raises ValueError (year 0 out of range), so _apply_merge/_apply_replace raise and the handler re-raises an unhandled 500. Self-impact only -> hardening.

local_checks.invariant: _validate_payload handles any JSON type for category_id without an unhandled exception.
local_checks.result: FAILS: category_types.get(category_id) raises TypeError (unhashable) when category_id is a JSON array/object; _validate_payload runs outside the try block, so it propagates as an unhandled 500. Self-impact only -> hardening.

hardening_notes: Import apply/validate can raise unhandled 500s on validator/sink disagreement: date year 0000 (valid_date_str passes, fromisoformat raises) and non-string category_id (TypeError unhashable). Both self-impact only. Fix: reject year < 1 and non-string category_id with the documented 422.

_read_body_within_limit uses declared.isdigit() then int(declared); a value passing str.isdigit() without being an int literal would raise ValueError -> 500. Likely rejected by the ASGI server first; not defensive.
Import note handling coerces any JSON value with str() and truncates to 140, unlike CRUD which rejects invalid notes; imported notes can carry Python repr artifacts.

final_decisions.note: Independently validated and refuted; retained in findings.json so future runs do not repeat the unsupported claim.

excluded_blocks.reason: No multi-tenant or access-controlled records: single-user store, so tenant-scope classes cannot apply.
No state machine, approval flow or replayable business flow beyond CRUD.
No cryptographic material, tokens or secrets in this unit.

local_checks.invariant: amount_cents is a positive int within PostgreSQL INTEGER range on every movement write path.
local_checks.result: create and update both call validate_amount (rejects bool/non-int/<=0/>MAX_CENTS); DB backstop is CheckConstraint amount_cents > 0. No write path bypasses it.

local_checks.invariant: movement.type must equal the referenced category.type and unknown categories are rejected.
local_checks.result: Both write paths call validate_category_match(type, category.type if category else None); missing category -> 'no existe', mismatch -> 'no corresponde'. Enforced application-side on every write path.

local_checks.invariant: PATCH validates the full resulting state (unset vs explicit null) and the date is a real calendar date; no state-machine/race/quantity bypass.
local_checks.result: MovementUpdate uses model_dump(exclude_unset=True); explicitly-null fields are re-validated and rejected with 422, unspecified fields retain stored values. valid_date_str enforces calendar validity incl. leap years. No ownership/expiry/uniqueness state exists; concurrent PATCH is last-write-wins by design for a single-user app.

excluded_blocks.reason: No cookies, sessions, tokens or identity layer exists; nothing for CSRF/session/fixation to bind to.
Target speaks plain HTTP/JSON with no second parser, proxy hop or cache key to desynchronize; nginx is the only front end.
No client-side sink in this unit; that is unit backend+frontend/render.
No dependency resolution or release handoff in this unit.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted movement fields reach no dangerous sink (SQL/shell/template/path/redirect/deserialization).
local_checks.result: Every DB access uses SQLAlchemy bound parameters; only literal SQL is the static text('SELECT 1') in main.py health and static server_default/Index text() in models.py. No subprocess/os.system/eval/exec/pickle/HTML sink exists on the path.

local_checks.invariant: Stored category_id/note/type are not re-used in a dangerous context by other backend code (second-order injection).
local_checks.result: Movement rows are read back only into typed Pydantic schemas and integer stats arithmetic; note is a plain Text column never concatenated into SQL/HTML/shell/log/header strings. category_id is validated via bound lookup.

excluded_blocks.reason: Single-user store; stats aggregate the one owner's records with no tenant scope.
Aggregations use bound parameters; month/end flow through month_bounds, not string SQL.

local_checks.invariant: summary/by-category/monthly aggregate the correct half-open month ranges and match the domain helpers.
local_checks.result: Holds. summary window [prev_start,start) matches average_prev_months offsets 1..6; by-category groups gasto sums over [start,end) filtering total>0; monthly uses shift_month(end,-(months-1)) over [start,end_exclusive) matching monthly_totals.

local_checks.invariant: No input accepted for month/end/months makes a stats handler raise an uncaught exception beyond the already-recorded month_bounds year-0000 gap.
local_checks.result: No distinct root cause. months bounded by Query(ge=1,le=24); end validated by month_bounds before shift_month -> 422; empty state yields total 0 / share 0.0 / 'na'. Year 0000 and '9999-12' 500 via the same month_bounds root cause already recorded -> not re-filed.

excluded_blocks.reason: No browser sink in a server-side CLI seed path.

local_checks.invariant: Seeding is idempotent and never destroys or overwrites real data when not forced.
local_checks.result: Does not hold for budgets (self-impact). _seed keys its guard only on the Movement count but also WRITES all 10 Budget.cap_cents; a DB with user budgets but zero movements will, on the next start with SEED_ON_START=true (compose default), re-inject the sample movements and reset every cap to sample values, contradicting docs/data-model.md rule 1.

local_checks.invariant: Seed-produced rows are valid under the same rules as CRUD/import.
local_checks.result: Holds for current constants (amounts <= 35,000,000 < MAX_CENTS, day <= 24 valid in all months, types/categories valid), but build_movements/_seed bypass validate_* entirely and the tables have no upper-bound CHECK, so re-tuning the re-tunable sample constants could introduce out-of-range values.

local_checks.invariant: Concurrent or mid-migration seeding cannot duplicate rows or run against a half-migrated schema.
local_checks.result: Non-atomic count-then-insert with no advisory lock; two concurrent runs against an empty table could double-insert. The maintained compose deployment runs one api service and seeds only after alembic upgrade head -> not realized by default.

hardening_notes: seed.py: the idempotency guard keys only on the Movement count while _seed also resets Budget.cap_cents; a DB with user budgets but zero movements re-seeds and overwrites caps on the next start (SEED_ON_START defaults true in compose), contradicting docs/data-model.md rule 1. Gate on an explicit already-seeded marker or also check budgets.

seed.py: build_movements/_seed bypass validate_* and the tables have no upper-bound CHECK; current constants are in-range but are explicitly re-tunable (data-model.md rule 6) with no defensive validation.

seed.py + entrypoint.sh: seeding and alembic upgrade are non-atomic/unlocked at container start; not realized under the single-instance default, but a second replica or a manual `make seed` during startup could race. Consider a Postgres advisory lock if scaled.

local_checks.invariant: Startup is fail-closed: migrations run before serving, DB-unavailable/migration failure aborts startup, no secret reaches the logs.
local_checks.result: Holds. set -euo pipefail; the wait loop exits 1 after DB_WAIT_TIMEOUT and omits both the exception and the URL; alembic upgrade head runs before uvicorn; uvicorn is exec'd last. alembic.ini leaves sqlalchemy.url empty and env.py resolves it at runtime with %-escaping, so no credentials live in the repo.

local_checks.invariant: Migration 0001 is re-runnable and its category data-seed is conflict-safe.
local_checks.result: Holds. _seed_categories uses pg_insert(...).on_conflict_do_nothing on PostgreSQL with an existence-check fallback; upgrade builds the schema with CHECKs/FKs/indexes and downgrade drops in FK-safe order; a re-run does not duplicate categories.

No admin/metrics/control-plane listener is started. Effective LAN reachability depends on the operator's .env and host firewall (not source-visible) - overlaps the compose-exposure unit.

local_checks.invariant: A repository-controlled ingress/listener must not expose an admin/debug/metrics/control-plane/internal API beyond the documented exposure posture.
local_checks.result: Established: db is unpublished; api publishes ${API_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${API_PORT:-8000}:8000 (loopback default); web publishes ${WEB_PORT:-8080}:8080 with no host-IP restriction, and nginx proxies all of /api/ (including /api/docs and /api/openapi.json) to the unauthenticated API. This is the documented, deliberate posture (README and docs/architecture.md). No admin/metrics/control-plane surface exists beyond the by-design full-data API. Actual LAN reachability depends on the host firewall and the operator's real .env, which are not source-visible.

hardening_notes: web is published as ${WEB_PORT:-8080}:8080 with no host-IP restriction, unlike api which honours API_BIND; consider a WEB_BIND control with a restricted default.
/api/docs and /api/openapi.json are reachable through the LAN-exposed web port with no toggle.
No container hardening on any service (no cap_drop, read_only rootfs, security_opt no-new-privileges, or userns remap).

excluded_blocks.block: WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md#Web cache poisoning through unkeyed input
excluded_blocks.reason: No upstream cache/CDN sits in front of nginx, and nginx does not cache proxied /api responses.
Frame protection is present (X-Frame-Options DENY plus CSP frame-ancestors none); no open UI-redress class.

local_checks.invariant: No response header is built from untrusted/request-controlled data with control characters or unsafe normalization.
local_checks.result: All add_header directives use static literals with 'always'; none interpolates a variable. proxy_set_header writes request context to the upstream (never into a response header) and the API never reads Host/X-Forwarded-*. No directive emits Location from request data; the SPA fallback is an internal try_files. Location blocks define no add_header, so server-level security headers are inherited (asserted by the integration smoke test).

hardening_notes: nginx sets nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options and CSP but not Strict-Transport-Security or Permissions-Policy; add them at the TLS terminator when exposing beyond localhost.
nginx forwards Host/X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-For/X-Forwarded-Proto but the app never reads them; if they ever become trust inputs, add a stripping ingress plus TrustedHostMiddleware.

local_checks.invariant: No API-controlled or browser-controlled string reaches an HTML/JS execution sink without framework escaping.
local_checks.result: Every /api/* JSON field is rendered through React JSX text/attribute binding only. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/outerHTML/document.write/eval/new Function/.html() exists. Notes render as JSX text and a React-controlled title attribute. Chart values are numeric geometry and constant palette strings. Only DOM construction is a Blob URL for the export download (not attacker-influenced HTML).
